title: Guard Your Eyes
devotional: What you repeatedly look at can influence what captures your attention and what remains in your thoughts. Jesus taught about the importance of what we allow into our lives through our eyes. Guarding your eyes does not mean being afraid of everything around you. It means becoming intentional about what you choose to keep watching. Some things may appear for a moment without your control. What matters is what you choose to continue looking at and feeding your attention. Today, practice turning away early instead of waiting until temptation becomes stronger.
mind_check: What type of visual content most often captures your attention and pulls your thoughts in an unhealthy direction?
body_move: Create physical distance from visual triggers. Close the page, put down the phone, unfollow the account, leave the room, or change what is on the screen.
spirit_move: Ask God for wisdom and self-control when you encounter something that pulls your attention away from Him. Turn your attention toward something that strengthens your faith.
way_out: When I see something that I know will pull me toward temptation, I will __________ immediately.
prayer: Father, help me become intentional about what I allow my eyes and attention to consume. Give me wisdom to recognize harmful influences and discipline to turn away quickly. Help me fill my mind with things that are true, pure, honorable, and pleasing to You. Amen.
action: Review the accounts, websites, apps, or types of content that regularly influence your thoughts. Remove, unfollow, mute, or limit at least one source that repeatedly pulls you in the wrong direction.
